1114 AplCore.fss
(* AplCore -- see AplCore.fsi.  The redesign of v1/base/AplCore.fss, promoted to
   the base on 2026-09-13: APL's values are Fortress's OWN arrays, not a wrapper.

   An APL scalar is an RR64; a vector is an Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] from
   array[\RR64\](n); a matrix is an Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] from
   array[\RR64\](r,c) (merged ledger row 57).  Rank is not a field, it is the
   TYPE, and every primitive is an overload family keyed on rank:

       f(x: RR64)                         rank 0
       f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])    rank 1
       f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])   rank 2

   This works -- and only this spelling works.  Overloading directly on
   Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] against Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] is rejected ("first
   parameters m:[...] and v:[...] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor
   equal)", r01_native.out), because two instantiations of one generic trait are
   not known to exclude.  Vector and Matrix reach Rank1 and Rank2, which DO
   exclude each other (FortressLibrary.fsi:1072-1076), and the nat is inferred
   from the runtime-built array (r02a_rankover.out).  Parameters are therefore
   Vector/Matrix; RESULTS are Array[\...\], the honest runtime-sized type.

   What the library does for us, for no lines at all: + and - elementwise on
   equal-length vectors and on matrices (Vector.+, Matrix.+), pmul, DOT, m.t(),
   |v|, v[i], m[i,j], u <- v, comprehensions, SUM, PROD, BIG MAX, and a LENGTH
   ERROR by dispatch when the two nats disagree (r09_reduce.out).

   Index origin is 0, as the chapter sets it with its first line, ⎕IO ← 0. *)
component AplCore
export AplCore

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- numbers ---- *)
(* RR64 -> ZZ32 in one line: there is still no narrowing (apl/gaps.md row 10),
   but the floor bracket's ZZ64 stringifies as an integer (row 11) and
   strToInt reads it back.  v1/base/AplCore.fss spent 14 lines on this. *)
aplInt(v: RR64): ZZ32 = strToInt("" (|\ v /|))

aplNegS(v: RR64): RR64 = -v

(* APL's high minus for negatives; integral values print without a fraction *)
aplFmt(v: RR64): String =
    if v < 0.0 then ("¯" aplFmt(-v))
    elif (1.0 (|\ v /|)) = v then ("" (|\ v /|))
    else ("" v) end

aplPad(s: String, w: ZZ32): String = do
    r: String := s
    while |r| < w do r := (" " r) end
    r
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------- constructors ----- *)
aplVec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
aplMat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
aplZilde(): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](0)

(* strand notation, built right to left by the grammar: the tail of a strand is
   a scalar when it has one element and a vector when it has more, so one
   overload each and no length bookkeeping in the grammar. *)
aplCons(x: RR64, y: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(2, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then x else y end)
aplCons[\nat s\](x: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|v| + 1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then x else v[i - 1] end)

(* ----------------------------------------------------------- display ----- *)
aplShow(x: RR64): String = aplFmt(x)

aplShow[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): String =
    if |v| = 0 then "" else (BIG |||[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] aplFmt(v[i])) end

(* Dyalog's matrix display: one line per row, each column padded to its own
   width (apl/gaps.md row 14, now over the library's own matrix). *)
aplShow[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    if (rows = 0) OR (cols = 0) then ""
    else
        w = array[\ZZ32\](cols).fill(
                fn (k: ZZ32): ZZ32 => BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] |aplFmt(m[i,k])|)
        BIG //[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ]
            (BIG |||[ k <- seq(0 # cols) ] aplPad(aplFmt(m[i,k]), w[k]))
    end
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------------- ⍳ iota ---- *)
aplIota(n: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { n >= 0.0 } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i)

(* --------------------------------------------------- ⍴ monadic: shape ---- *)
aplShapeOf(x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZilde()
aplShapeOf[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 |v|)
aplShapeOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(2, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then 1.0 rows else 1.0 cols end)
  end

(* --------------------------------------------------- ⍴ dyadic: reshape --- *)
(* The RESULT's rank is the LENGTH of the left argument, a runtime value -- the
   one place where APL's rank is not in the type.  The grammar reads it off the
   source text instead: `2 4⍴x` fires aplReshapeM, `4⍴x` fires aplReshapeV, so
   the rank is fixed at expansion time and never at run time. *)
aplReshapeV(n: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { n >= 0.0 } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplReshapeV[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { (n >= 0.0) AND (|v| > 0) } =
    aplVec(aplInt(n), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => v[i MOD |v|])

aplReshapeM(rw: RR64, cl: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) } =
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), aplInt(cl), fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplReshapeM[\nat s\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) AND (|v| > 0) } = do
    c = aplInt(cl)
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), c, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => v[((c i) + j) MOD |v|])
  end
aplReshapeM[\nat r, nat c\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) } = do
    (mr, mc) = m.sizes
    cc = aplInt(cl)
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), cc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => do
        k = ((cc i) + j) MOD (mr mc)
        m[k DIV mc, k MOD mc]
      end)
  end

(* ------------------------------------------- scalar extension: × ÷ + - --- *)
(* + and - between two vectors, or two matrices, are the library's own
   (Vector.+, Matrix.+) and cost nothing here.  What the library does not have
   is APL's scalar extension, nor an elementwise × or ÷, so those are declared
   -- as real operators, both arities, so that the monadic/dyadic split of APL
   is just Fortress overloading (r04_glyphs.out: × ÷ - ⊖ ⊂ ⊃ ≡ ≢ * and ∘ all
   take a prefix AND an infix declaration; , ⌈ ⌊ do not). *)
opr ×[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i] b[i])
opr ×[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a x)
opr ×[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x a)
(* monadic × is APL's signum *)
opr ×(x: RR64): RR64 = if x > 0.0 then 1.0 elif x < 0.0 then -1.0 else 0.0 end
opr ×[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => × x)

opr ÷(a: RR64, b: RR64): RR64 = a / b
opr ÷[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => a[i] / b[i])
opr ÷[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a / x)
opr ÷[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x / a)
opr ÷(x: RR64): RR64 = 1.0 / x
opr ÷[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => 1.0 / x)

opr +[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a + x)
opr +[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x + a)
opr +[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a + x)

opr -[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a - x)
opr -[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x - a)

(* APL's dyadic * is power; the host's * is free (it is not multiplication --
   that is juxtaposition).  Watch the use site:
   an open parenthesis immediately followed by the star opens a COMMENT, and
   Fortress comments nest, so a space is needed after the parenthesis
   (r05f_starparen.out). *)
opr *(a: RR64, b: RR64): RR64 = a^b
opr *[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => x^a)
opr *[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => a^x)

(* ------------------------------------------------- ⌈ ⌊ : MAX, MIN, ceil -- *)
(* ⌈ and ⌉ are ENCLOSERS in the host table (operators.tex:67-70), so neither
   arity of ⌈ is declarable: r05b_ceil.out is `Unmatched delimiter "|/"`.  The
   dyadic glyph therefore expands to the host's MAX/MIN and the monadic one to
   a named function -- the grammar still reads APL's glyph. *)
opr MAX[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if a[i] > b[i] then a[i] else b[i] end)
opr MAX[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => if a > x then a else x end)
opr MIN[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if a[i] < b[i] then a[i] else b[i] end)
opr MIN[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => if a < x then a else x end)

aplCeil(x: RR64): RR64 = 1.0 (|/ x \|)
aplCeil[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => 1.0 (|/ x \|))
aplFloor(x: RR64): RR64 = 1.0 (|\ x /|)
aplFloor[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =

aplFloor[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => 1.0 (|\ x /|))

(* ---------------------------------------------- ≡ match, ≢ tally/notmatch - *)
(* ≡ and ≢ are in the host table (EQV, NEQV) and take both arities.  APL's
   match compares shape first, so the cross-rank cases are separate overloads:
   six of them for three ranks, the price of putting rank in the type. *)
opr ≡(a: RR64, b: RR64): RR64 = if a = b then 1.0 else 0.0 end
opr ≡[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): RR64 =
    if |a| =/= |b| then 0.0
    elif |a| = 0 then 1.0
    elif (BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # |a|) ] (if a[i] = b[i] then 0.0 else 1.0 end)) > 0.0
    then 0.0 else 1.0 end
opr ≡[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): RR64 = do
    (ar, ac) = a.sizes
    (br, bc) = b.sizes
    if (ar =/= br) OR (ac =/= bc) then 0.0
    elif (BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # ar), j <- seq(0 # ac) ]
            (if a[i,j] = b[i,j] then 0.0 else 1.0 end)) > 0.0
    then 0.0 else 1.0 end
  end
opr ≡[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = 0.0
opr ≡[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = 0.0
opr ≡[\nat s\](a: RR64, b: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = 0.0
opr ≡[\nat s\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: RR64): RR64 = 0.0

opr ≢(x: RR64): RR64 = 1.0
opr ≢[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = 1.0 |v|
opr ≢[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; 1.0 rows end

(* -------------------------------------------------------- ⊃ first -------- *)
opr ⊃(x: RR64): RR64 = x
opr ⊃[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = if |v| = 0 then 0.0 else v[0] end
opr ⊃[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = m[0,0]

(* ------------------------------------------------ ⌽ ⊖ reverse, ⍉ transpose *)
(* ⌽ ⍉ ⍳ ⍴ ⍋ ⍒ are not in the host operator table at all, so they stay named
   functions; ⊖ is (OMINUS) and is an operator. *)
aplRev(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplRev[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|v|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => v[(|v| - 1) - i])
aplRev[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i, (cols - 1) - j])
  end

opr ⊖(x: RR64): RR64 = x
opr ⊖[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplRev(v)
opr ⊖[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[(rows - 1) - i, j])
  end

aplTrans(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplTrans[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v
(* the library already owns this one *)
aplTrans[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.t()

(* --------------------------------------------------- , catenate, ravel --- *)
(* , is the argument separator and cannot be an operator in EITHER arity:
   r05a_comma.out (infix) and r05e_ravel.out (prefix) are both a bare
   `Syntax Error` at the declaration.  So catenate and ravel are named. *)
aplCat(a: RR64, b: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplCons(a, b)
aplCat[\nat s\](a: RR64, b: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplCons(a, b)
aplCat[\nat s\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|a| + 1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < |a| then a[i] else b end)
aplCat[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|a| + |b|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < |a| then a[i] else b[i - |a|] end)

aplRavel(x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplVec(1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplRavel[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = v
aplRavel[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows cols, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => m[k DIV cols, k MOD cols])
  end

(* ------------------------------------------- comparison: APL's 0/1 ------- *)
(* A host comparison returns a Boolean; APL's returns a 0/1 array.  The glyph
   can be redeclared with the APL result type (r06_hostops.out) -- the numeric
   overload is more specific than the library's Boolean one and wins. *)
opr =[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if a[i] = b[i] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
opr ≤[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if a[i] <= b[i] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)

(* ------------------------------------------------------ reductions ------- *)
(* f/ reduces along the LAST axis, f⌿ along the FIRST; on a vector both are the
   same fold.  The body is the library's own big operator wherever the library
   has one (SUM, PROD, BIG MAX -- no `except { opr BIG + }` needed, ledger row
   41, because RR64 is already a Number), and a hand fold only for -/ , which
   is not associative and has no big operator.  An axis reduction of a matrix
   is a fill over the other axis: an ARRAY comprehension would be the natural
   spelling and is dead at two layers (ledger row 50), and a row VIEW would
   carry no algebra (rows 54, 56). *)
aplSumLast(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplSumLast[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = SUM[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] v[i]
aplSumLast[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[ j <- seq(0 # cols) ] m[i,j])
  end
aplSumFirst(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplSumFirst[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = aplSumLast(v)
aplSumFirst[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(cols, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] m[i,k])
  end

aplProdLast(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplProdLast[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = PROD[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] v[i]
aplProdLast[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => PROD[ j <- seq(0 # cols) ] m[i,j])
  end

aplMaxLast(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplMaxLast[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] v[i]
aplMaxLast[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MAX[ j <- seq(0 # cols) ] m[i,j])
  end

aplDifLast(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplDifLast[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = do
    acc: RR64 := v[|v| - 1]
    j: ZZ32 := |v| - 2
    while j >= 0 do acc := v[j] - acc; j := j - 1 end
    acc
  end
aplDifLast[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => do
        acc: RR64 := m[i, cols - 1]
        j: ZZ32 := cols - 2
        while j >= 0 do acc := m[i,j] - acc; j := j - 1 end
        acc
      end)
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------- character arrays ------ *)
(* An APL character array is an Array[\Char,ZZ32\].  It may NOT join the numeric
   overload family: a Char vector parameter beside an RR64 one is rejected,
   "at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"
   (r07_edge.out), because Array1[\Char,0,s\] and Vector[\RR64,s\] are both
   Rank1 and neither excludes the other.  So the character primitives carry
   their own NAMES -- one extra name per primitive that admits characters --
   and APL's DOMAIN ERROR on 'abc'+1 is the numeric family failing to dispatch
   (r08_edge.out, "Failed to find any matching overload"). *)
aplChars(s: String): Array[\Char,ZZ32\] =
    array[\Char\](|s|).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): Char => s[i])
aplShowC[\nat s\](v: Array1[\Char,0,s\]): String =
    if |v| = 0 then "" else (BIG ||[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] ("" v[i])) end
aplTallyC[\nat s\](v: Array1[\Char,0,s\]): RR64 = 1.0 |v|


(* ======================================================== rung 2: indexing ==
   See AplCore.fsi for the rule that shapes every signature here.  Three facts
   from s01_ix.fss, all on the native carrier and all load-bearing:

   (a) a library array is MUTABLE through a Vector/Matrix parameter -- v.put(i,x)
       and m.put((i,j),x) -- so APL's indexed and selective assignment are
       in-place puts.  That is what lets an APL variable be a plain lambda
       parameter: the name never has to be rebound (apl gap row 29 says it
       cannot be) and nothing is copied.
   (b) the library's own row view m[1,:] is NOT an AnyVector (merged ledger
       row 54, re-confirmed here over a runtime-sized matrix), so it carries no
       vector algebra; but a 6-line user object extending Vector (row 55) is one,
       and its nat parameters are inferred from the runtime-built matrix.  So
       m[1;] and m[;1] are zero-copy views with the full algebra.
   (c) RR64 excludes Array1 (FortressLibrary.fsi:1435), so a scalar index and a
       vector index are an excluding pair and the rank of an indexed result is
       settled by overload resolution. *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------- row/column views -- *)
object AplRow[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(j: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), v)
    init0(j: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), v)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
object AplCol[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,r\]
    get(i: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(i: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), v)
    init0(i: ZZ32, v: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), v)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,r\] = array1[\U,r\]()
end

(* ---------------------------------------------------- bracket indexing ----- *)
(* An out-of-range index is APL's INDEX ERROR, as a contract violation. *)
aplIx1[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: RR64): RR64
        requires { (i >= 0.0) AND (i < (1.0 |v|)) } = v[aplInt(i)]
aplIx1[\nat s, nat t\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|i|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => v[aplInt(i[k])])

aplIx2[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64, j: RR64): RR64 =
    m[aplInt(i), aplInt(j)]
aplIx2[\nat r, nat c, nat t\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64, j: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|j|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(i), aplInt(j[k])])
aplIx2[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: Vector[\RR64,s\], j: RR64):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|i|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(i[k]), aplInt(j)])
aplIx2[\nat r, nat c, nat s, nat t\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: Vector[\RR64,s\],
        j: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplMat(|i|, |j|, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(i[a]), aplInt(j[b])])

aplIxRow[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64): Vector[\RR64,c\] =
    AplRow[\r,c\](m, aplInt(i))
aplIxRow[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: Vector[\RR64,s\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(|i|, cols, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(i[a]), b])
  end
aplIxCol[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: RR64): Vector[\RR64,r\] =
    AplCol[\r,c\](m, aplInt(j))
aplIxCol[\nat r, nat c, nat t\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, |j|, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[a, aplInt(j[b])])
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------ ⊂ coordinates, scatter --- *)
aplPick[\nat s, nat t\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: Vector[\RR64,t\]): RR64 = v[aplInt(i[0])]
aplPick[\nat r, nat c, nat t\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: Vector[\RR64,t\]): RR64 =
    m[aplInt(i[0]), aplInt(i[1])]

aplIdxOne[\nat s\](c: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplMat(1, |c|, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => c[b])
aplIdxCons[\nat s, nat p, nat q\](c: Vector[\RR64,s\], rest: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = rest.sizes
    aplMat(rows + 1, cols,
           fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => if a = 0 then c[b] else rest[a - 1, b] end)
  end
aplScatter[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], cs: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (k, rank) = cs.sizes
    aplVec(k, fn (a: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(cs[a,0]), aplInt(cs[a,1])])
  end

(* ----------------------------------------------------------- ⌷ squad ------- *)
aplSquad1[\nat s\](i: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = v[aplInt(i)]
aplSquad1[\nat r, nat c\](i: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Vector[\RR64,c\] =
    AplRow[\r,c\](m, aplInt(i))
aplSquad2[\nat r, nat c\](i: RR64, j: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 =
    m[aplInt(i), aplInt(j)]
aplSquadEncl[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](i: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(|i|, cols, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(i[a]), b])
  end

(* ----------------------------------------------------------- ⍸ where ------- *)
(* Rung 3 widens this from Boolean to COUNTS, which is what APL's ⍸ always was:
   index k appears v[k] times, so ⍸0 1 0 2 0 3 … is 1 3 3 5 5 5 … (the chapter's
   Ex 27).  A 0/1 argument behaves exactly as it did in rung 2. *)
aplWhere[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    n: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |v| do n := n + aplInt(v[k]); k := k + 1 end
    out = array[\RR64\](n).fill(0.0)
    p: ZZ32 := 0
    k := 0
    while k < |v| do
        j: ZZ32 := 0
        while j < aplInt(v[k]) do out.put(p, 1.0 k); p := p + 1; j := j + 1 end
        k := k + 1
    end
    out
  end

(* ------------------------------------------- / ⌿ compress and replicate ---- *)
aplRepCount[\nat s\](sel: Vector[\RR64,s\]): ZZ32 = do
    n: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |sel| do n := n + aplInt(sel[k]); k := k + 1 end
    n
  end

aplCompress[\nat s, nat t\](sel: Vector[\RR64,s\], d: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { |sel| = |d| } = do
    out = array[\RR64\](aplRepCount(sel)).fill(0.0)
    p: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |sel| do
        j: ZZ32 := 0
        while j < aplInt(sel[k]) do out.put(p, d[k]); p := p + 1; j := j + 1 end
        k := k + 1
    end
    out
  end
aplCompress[\nat t\](sel: RR64, d: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplCompress(aplVec(|d|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => sel), d)
aplCompress[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](sel: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    which = aplCompress(sel, aplVec(|sel|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 k))
    aplMat(rows, |which|, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[a, aplInt(which[b])])
  end
aplCompressFirst[\nat s, nat t\](sel: Vector[\RR64,s\], d: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { |sel| = |d| } = aplCompress(sel, d)
aplCompressFirst[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](sel: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    which = aplCompress(sel, aplVec(|sel|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 k))
    aplMat(|which|, cols, fn (a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplInt(which[a]), b])
  end

(* --------------------------------- indexed and selective assignment, in place *)
aplIxPut1[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: RR64, x: RR64): ()
        requires { (i >= 0.0) AND (i < (1.0 |v|)) } = v.put(aplInt(i), x)
aplIxPut1[\nat s, nat t\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: Vector[\RR64,t\], x: RR64): () = do
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |i| do v.put(aplInt(i[k]), x); k := k + 1 end
  end
aplIxPut1[\nat s, nat t, nat u\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], i: Vector[\RR64,t\],
        x: Vector[\RR64,u\]): () requires { |i| = |x| } = do
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |i| do v.put(aplInt(i[k]), x[k]); k := k + 1 end
  end

end
aplIxPut2[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64, j: RR64, x: RR64): () =
    m.put((aplInt(i), aplInt(j)), x)
aplIxPutRow[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64, x: RR64): () = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < cols do m.put((aplInt(i), k), x); k := k + 1 end
  end
aplIxPutRow[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: RR64, x: Vector[\RR64,s\]): ()
        = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < cols do m.put((aplInt(i), k), x[k MOD |x|]); k := k + 1 end
  end
aplIxPutCol[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: RR64, x: RR64): () = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < rows do m.put((k, aplInt(j)), x); k := k + 1 end
  end
aplIxPutCol[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], j: RR64, x: Vector[\RR64,s\]): ()
        = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < rows do m.put((k, aplInt(j)), x[k MOD |x|]); k := k + 1 end
  end

(* (select/data) ← ¯1 ¯1 ¯1 ¯1 ¯1 : the selected positions take the successive
   elements of the right argument.  APL inverts an arbitrary expression on the
   left of ←; a template grammar needs one production and one function per
   invertible shape, and these two are the chapter's. *)
aplSelPut[\nat s, nat t, nat u\](d: Vector[\RR64,s\], sel: Vector[\RR64,t\],
        x: Vector[\RR64,u\]): () requires { |sel| = |d| } = do
    p: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |sel| do
        if sel[k] =/= 0.0 then d.put(k, x[p MOD |x|]); p := p + 1 end
        k := k + 1
    end
  end
(* APL extends a scalar right argument over the selection.  Without this overload
   `(select/data) ← ¯1` is not an APL error but a host "Unification error: Cannot
   unify Float with Vector[\RR64,u\]" reported against AplSyntax.fsi:1:1
   (Rung2.out.1 -- gap row 35's span again). *)
aplSelPut[\nat s, nat t\](d: Vector[\RR64,s\], sel: Vector[\RR64,t\], x: RR64): ()
        requires { |sel| = |d| } = do
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |sel| do
        if sel[k] =/= 0.0 then d.put(k, x) end
        k := k + 1
    end
  end

(* (0 0⍉m) ← ¯1 ¯1 ¯1 : 0 0⍉m is the main diagonal *)
aplDiagPut[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], x: Vector[\RR64,s\]): () = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    n = if rows < cols then rows else cols end
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < n do m.put((k, k), x[k MOD |x|]); k := k + 1 end
  end

(* ======================================================= rung 3: glyphiary ==
   The chapter's primitives, each an overload family on the ranks.  Three
   things decided the shapes below, all measured in ../rung-3/:

   (a) every glyph of the chapter that is not an encloser CAN be declared as an
       opr in both arities -- ≠ < > ≥ ∧ ∨, a dyadic ⊖ beside the monadic one,
       and a PREFIX * (t01_ops.out).  Only ⌈ ⌊ | , stay named, as in rung 1.
   (b) the library already owns matrix + and matrix - (Matrix.+ / Matrix.-,
       FortressLibrary.fsi:1581-1582), so those are NOT redeclared; it owns no
       elementwise ×, ÷ or *, so those are.
   (c) AND is STRICT -- `opr AND(a:Boolean, b:Boolean)` beside
       `opr AND(a:Boolean, b:()->Boolean)`, and an ordinary `a AND b` takes the
       first (t03_and.out) -- so no loop guard here may lean on it to keep an
       index in range; the grades below break out of the inner loop instead. *)

(* the two shape readers the contracts below are written in terms of: a
   `requires` clause cannot destructure m.sizes *)
aplRowsOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): ZZ32 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; rows end
aplColsOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): ZZ32 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; cols end

(* --------------------------------------------- the elementwise skeletons --- *)
(* Every comparison, every Boolean connective and every matrix arithmetic op is
   one of these six zips with a scalar function, so each opr below is one line. *)
aplZipV[\nat s, nat t\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { |a| = |b| } =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i], b[i]))
aplZipSV[\nat s\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(a, x))
aplZipVS[\nat s\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    v.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(x, a))
aplZipM[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\],
        b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (aplRowsOf(a) = aplRowsOf(b)) AND (aplColsOf(a) = aplColsOf(b)) } = do
    (ar, ac) = a.sizes
    aplMat(ar, ac, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => f(a[i,j], b[i,j]))
  end
aplZipSM[\nat r, nat c\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(a, x))
aplZipMS[\nat r, nat c\](f: (RR64,RR64)->RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m.map[\RR64\](fn (x: RR64): RR64 => f(x, a))

(* the scalar kernels; APL's comparisons yield 0/1, not a Boolean *)
aplEqS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x = y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplNeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x =/= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplLtS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x < y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplLeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x <= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplGtS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplGeS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x >= y then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplAndS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if (x =/= 0.0) AND (y =/= 0.0) then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplOrS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if (x =/= 0.0) OR (y =/= 0.0) then 1.0 else 0.0 end
aplMaxS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x > y then x else y end
aplMinS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = if x < y then x else y end
aplMulS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x y
aplDivS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x / y
aplSubS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x - y
aplAddS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x + y
aplPowS(x: RR64, y: RR64): RR64 = x^y
(* APL's residue: a|b is b modulo a and takes the SIGN OF A; 0|b is b *)
aplResS(a: RR64, b: RR64): RR64 = if a = 0.0 then b else b - (a (1.0 (|\ b / a /|))) end

(* ------------------------------------------------------- comparisons ------ *)
(* (s,s) is deliberately NOT declared: a scalar comparison stays the library's
   Boolean one (gap row 41), so `2<3` is a host Boolean and not APL's 1. *)
opr =[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplEqS, a, v)
opr =[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplEqS, v, a)
opr =[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplZipM(aplEqS, a, b)
opr =[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipSM(aplEqS, a, m)
opr =[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipMS(aplEqS, m, a)

opr ≠[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplZipV(aplNeS, a, b)
opr ≠[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplNeS, a, v)
opr ≠[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplNeS, v, a)
opr ≠[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplZipM(aplNeS, a, b)
opr ≠[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipSM(aplNeS, a, m)
opr ≠[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipMS(aplNeS, m, a)

opr <[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplZipV(aplLtS, a, b)
opr <[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplLtS, a, v)
opr <[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplLtS, v, a)
opr <[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplZipM(aplLtS, a, b)
opr <[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipSM(aplLtS, a, m)
opr <[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipMS(aplLtS, m, a)

opr ≤[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplLeS, a, v)
opr ≤[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplLeS, v, a)
opr ≤[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplZipM(aplLeS, a, b)
opr ≤[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipSM(aplLeS, a, m)
opr ≤[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipMS(aplLeS, m, a)

opr >[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplZipV(aplGtS, a, b)
opr >[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplGtS, a, v)
opr >[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplGtS, v, a)
opr >[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplZipM(aplGtS, a, b)
opr >[\nat r, nat c\](a: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipSM(aplGtS, a, m)
opr >[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplZipMS(aplGtS, m, a)

opr ≥[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplZipV(aplGeS, a, b)
opr ≥[\nat s\](a: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipSV(aplGeS, a, v)
opr ≥[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], a: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplZipVS(aplGeS, v, a)
opr ≥[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):

(* -------------------------------------------------------- ↑ take, ↓ drop -- *)
(* A negative count takes (drops) from the back; an overtake pads with the
   numeric prototype 0.  The rank of the result is the rank of the argument, so
   1↑mat is a one-row MATRIX and not a vector. *)
aplTake(n: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplTake(n, aplVec(1, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => x))
aplTake[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    k = aplInt(n)
    if k >= 0 then aplVec(k, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < |v| then v[i] else 0.0 end)
    else do
        kk = -k
        aplVec(kk, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => do
            j = (|v| - kk) + i
            if (j >= 0) AND (j < |v|) then v[j] else 0.0 end
          end)
      end
    end
  end
aplTake[\nat r, nat c\](n: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k = aplInt(n)
    if k >= 0 then
        aplMat(k, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < rows then m[i,j] else 0.0 end)
    else do
        kk = -k
        aplMat(kk, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => do
            p = (rows - kk) + i
            if (p >= 0) AND (p < rows) then m[p,j] else 0.0 end
          end)
      end
    end
  end
aplTake[\nat r, nat c\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    a = aplInt(rw)
    b = aplInt(cl)
    ra = if a >= 0 then a else -a end
    rb = if b >= 0 then b else -b end
    oi = if a >= 0 then 0 else rows - ra end
    oj = if b >= 0 then 0 else cols - rb end
    aplMat(ra, rb, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => do
        p = oi + i
        q = oj + j
        if (p >= 0) AND (p < rows) then
            (if (q >= 0) AND (q < cols) then m[p,q] else 0.0 end)
        else 0.0 end
      end)
  end

aplDrop[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    k = aplInt(n)
    kk = if k >= 0 then k else -k end
    left = if kk > |v| then 0 else |v| - kk end
    off = if k >= 0 then kk else 0 end
    aplVec(left, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => v[i + off])
  end
aplDrop[\nat r, nat c\](n: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k = aplInt(n)
    kk = if k >= 0 then k else -k end
    left = if kk > rows then 0 else rows - kk end
    off = if k >= 0 then kk else 0 end
    aplMat(left, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i + off, j])
  end
aplDrop[\nat r, nat c\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    a = aplInt(rw)
    b = aplInt(cl)
    ra = if a >= 0 then a else -a end
    rb = if b >= 0 then b else -b end
    nr = if ra > rows then 0 else rows - ra end
    nc = if rb > cols then 0 else cols - rb end
    oi = if a >= 0 then ra else 0 end
    oj = if b >= 0 then rb else 0 end
    aplMat(nr, nc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i + oi, j + oj])
  end

(* --------------------------------------------------- ⌽ and ⊖ with a count - *)
aplRotN(i: ZZ32, k: ZZ32, n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = ((((i + k) MOD n) + n) MOD n)
aplRotate[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    k = aplInt(n)
    aplVec(|v|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => v[aplRotN(i, k, |v|)])
  end
(* a count rotates each ROW of a matrix: ⌽ is the LAST axis *)
aplRotate[\nat r, nat c\](n: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k = aplInt(n)
    aplMat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i, aplRotN(j, k, cols)])
  end
(* ⊖ is the FIRST axis; a VECTOR left argument rotates each column by its own
   count (the chapter's 1 2 ¯1 0⊖mat) *)
opr ⊖[\nat s\](n: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplRotate(n, v)
opr ⊖[\nat r, nat c\](n: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    k = aplInt(n)
    aplMat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplRotN(i, k, rows), j])
  end
opr ⊖[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](ks: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { |ks| = aplColsOf(m) } = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[aplRotN(i, aplInt(ks[j]), rows), j])
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------- ⍳ index of, ⍸ interval - *)
(* not found is ≢⍺, which with ⎕IO ← 0 is the length of the left argument *)
aplIndexOf[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], x: RR64): RR64 = do
    hit: ZZ32 := |v|
    k: ZZ32 := |v| - 1
    while k >= 0 do (if v[k] = x then hit := k end); k := k - 1 end
    1.0 hit
  end
aplIndexOf[\nat s, nat t\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], w: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|w|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => aplIndexOf(v, w[k]))

(* dyadic ⍸: the index of the interval a value falls in, boundaries going to the
   higher bin and anything below the first bin giving ⎕IO-1, here ¯1 *)
aplBin[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], x: RR64): RR64 = do
    n: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |v| do (if v[k] <= x then n := n + 1 end); k := k + 1 end
    1.0 (n - 1)
  end
aplBin[\nat s, nat t\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], w: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|w|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => aplBin(v, w[k]))

(* ------------------------------------------------- ∊ ∪ ∩ ~ set primitives - *)
aplIn[\nat s\](x: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = do
    hit: RR64 := 0.0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |v| do (if v[k] = x then hit := 1.0 end); k := k + 1 end
    hit
  end
aplIn[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplVec(|a|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => aplIn(a[k], b))
aplIn[\nat r, nat c\](x: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = aplIn(x, aplRavel(m))

(* monadic ∊ is Enlist; on a simple array it is Ravel *)
aplEnlist(x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplRavel(x)
aplEnlist[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplRavel(v)
aplEnlist[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = aplRavel(m)

(* Dyalog's Union KEEPS the left argument's duplicates and appends the elements
   of the right that are not already present *)
aplUnion[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    keep = array[\RR64\](|b|).fill(0.0)
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |b| do
        fresh = if aplIn(b[k], a) =/= 0.0 then 0.0
                else (if aplIn(b[k], aplTake(1.0 k, b)) =/= 0.0 then 0.0 else 1.0 end) end
        keep.put(k, fresh)
        k := k + 1
    end
    aplCat(a, aplCompress(keep, b))
  end
aplUnique[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    keep = array[\RR64\](|v|).fill(0.0)
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while k < |v| do
        keep.put(k, if aplIn(v[k], aplTake(1.0 k, v)) =/= 0.0 then 0.0 else 1.0 end)
        k := k + 1
    end
    aplCompress(keep, v)
  end
aplIntersect[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplCompress(aplIn(a, b), a)
aplWithout[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplCompress(aplVec(|a|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 - aplIn(a[k], b)), a)
aplWithout[\nat s\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], x: RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplCompress(aplVec(|a|, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => if a[k] = x then 0.0 else 1.0 end), a)
aplNot(x: RR64): RR64 = 1.0 - x
aplNot[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =

(* ----------------------------------------------- , and ⍪ over two ranks --- *)
aplCat[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { aplRowsOf(a) = aplRowsOf(b) } = do
    (ar, ac) = a.sizes
    (br, bc) = b.sizes
    aplMat(ar, ac + bc,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j < ac then a[i,j] else b[i, j - ac] end)
  end
aplCat[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], v: Vector[\RR64,s\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { |v| = aplRowsOf(m) } = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols + 1,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j < cols then m[i,j] else v[i] end)
  end
aplCat[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { |v| = aplRowsOf(m) } = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols + 1,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j = 0 then v[i] else m[i, j - 1] end)
  end
aplCat[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], x: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows, cols + 1,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j < cols then m[i,j] else x end)
  end

aplCatFirst[\nat s, nat t\](a: Vector[\RR64,s\], b: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    aplCat(a, b)
aplCatFirst[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { aplColsOf(a) = aplColsOf(b) } = do
    (ar, ac) = a.sizes
    (br, bc) = b.sizes
    aplMat(ar + br, ac,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < ar then a[i,j] else b[i - ar, j] end)
  end
aplCatFirst[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { |v| = aplColsOf(m) } = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows + 1, cols,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if i = 0 then v[j] else m[i - 1, j] end)
  end
aplCatFirst[\nat r, nat c, nat s\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], v: Vector[\RR64,s\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { |v| = aplColsOf(m) } = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplMat(rows + 1, cols,
           fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if i < rows then m[i,j] else v[j] end)
  end

(* monadic ⍪ is Table: the argument as a matrix, one row per major cell *)
aplTable(x: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = aplMat(1, 1, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplTable[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplMat(|v|, 1, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => v[i])
aplTable[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = m

(* -------------------------------------------------------- ⍋ ⍒ grades ----- *)
(* A stable insertion sort of the INDEX vector: equal elements keep their
   original order, which is what the chapter's ⍋data shows for its two 18s.
   The inner loop cannot be a `while (j > 0) AND (…v[idx[j-1]]…)`: AND is strict
   (t03_and.out), and the second operand would index at ¯1. *)
aplGradeUp[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    n = |v|
    idx = array[\RR64\](n).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i)
    i: ZZ32 := 1
    while i < n do
        j: ZZ32 := i
        while j > 0 do
            if v[aplInt(idx[j - 1])] > v[aplInt(idx[j])] then
                t = idx[j - 1]
                idx.put(j - 1, idx[j])
                idx.put(j, t)
                j := j - 1
            else j := 0 end
        end
        i := i + 1
    end
    idx
  end
aplGradeDown[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    n = |v|
    idx = array[\RR64\](n).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i)
    i: ZZ32 := 1
    while i < n do
        j: ZZ32 := i
        while j > 0 do
            if v[aplInt(idx[j - 1])] < v[aplInt(idx[j])] then
                t = idx[j - 1]
                idx.put(j - 1, idx[j])
                idx.put(j, t)
                j := j - 1
            else j := 0 end
        end
        i := i + 1
    end
    idx
  end

(* ------------------------------------------- the missing reductions ------- *)
aplMinLast(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplMinLast[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = BIG MIN[ i <- seq(0 # |v|) ] v[i]
aplMinLast[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(rows, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MIN[ j <- seq(0 # cols) ] m[i,j])
  end
aplMinFirst(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplMinFirst[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = aplMinLast(v)
aplMinFirst[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(cols, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MIN[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] m[i,k])
  end
aplMaxFirst(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplMaxFirst[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = aplMaxLast(v)
aplMaxFirst[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(cols, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MAX[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] m[i,k])
  end
aplProdFirst(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplProdFirst[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = aplProdLast(v)
aplProdFirst[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    aplVec(cols, fn (k: ZZ32): RR64 => PROD[ i <- seq(0 # rows) ] m[i,k])
  end

end

(* u07: rank 3.  The APL-in-Fortress base dispatches every primitive on the
   PARAMETER's rank -- RR64 / Vector[\RR64,s\] / Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] -- because
   Rank1 and Rank2 exclude each other.  FortressLibrary.fss:1592-1606 declares a
   Rank3 in the same family, so the question is whether the rank-3 analogue is
   available and whether it joins the same overload family.

   (a) array3 with literal nats
   (b) a RUNTIME-sized rank-3 array: array[\RR64\](x,y,z), library line 1925
   (c) t[i,j,k] := and t[i,j,k], and the extents
   (d) the overload family f : RR64 / Vector / Matrix / Array3
   (e) which one a runtime-built rank-3 array picks
   (f) what the rank-3 analogue of Vector/Matrix is -- array1 and array2 route
       numeric element types to vector[] and matrix[] (library lines 2240-2246
       and 2599-2603); array3 does not.
   (g) .fill with a three-argument function.  Note that the library's own
       array3[\T,s0,s1,s2\](f) overload (FortressLibrary.fss:2818) declares its
       argument as (ZZ32,ZZ32)->T, a two-argument function, which cannot be what
       Array3.fill wants; .fill is the working route. *)
component u07_rank3
import AplCore.{...}
export Executable

f(x: RR64): String = "rank 0"
f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): String = "rank 1, " |v| " elements"
f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = "rank 2, " r "x" c
f[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): String =
    "rank 3, " a "x" b "x" c

run(): () = do
    println("(a) array3 with literal nats:")
    t0 = array3[\RR64, 2, 3, 4\](0.0)
    println(("  t0.sizes = " t0.sizes ", |t0| = " |t0|))

    println("(b) a runtime-sized rank-3 array from array[\\RR64\\](x,y,z):")
    x = 2; y = 3; z = 4
    t = array[\RR64\](x, y, z)
    println(("  t.sizes = " t.sizes))

    println("(c) put, get, extents:")
    for i <- seq(0 # x), j <- seq(0 # y), k <- seq(0 # z) do
        t[i,j,k] := 1.0 ((i (y z)) + (j z) + k)
    end
    println(("  t[1,2,3] = " t[1,2,3]))
    println(("  t[0,0,0] = " t[0,0,0]))
    (a0,a1,a2) = t.sizes
    println(("  extents  = " a0 " " a1 " " a2))

    println("(d)(e) the overload family:")
    println(("  f(3.0)                 -> " f(3.0)))
    println(("  f(aplVec(5,...))       -> " f(aplVec(5, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 i))))
    println(("  f(aplMat(2,3,...))     -> " f(aplMat(2, 3, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.0))))
    println(("  f(array[\\RR64\\](2,3,4)) -> " f(t)))
    println(("  f(array3 literal nats) -> " f(t0)))

    println("(f) what the runtime-built rank-3 array IS:")
    typecase t of
        Rank3 => println("  it is a Rank3")
        else  => println("  it is NOT a Rank3")
    end
    typecase t of
        AnyVector => println("  it is an AnyVector")
        AnyMatrix => println("  it is an AnyMatrix")
        else      => println("  it is neither AnyVector nor AnyMatrix")
    end

    println("(g) filling by function:")
    t2 = array[\RR64\](2,2,2).fill(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 =>
                                       1.0 ((4 i) + (2 j) + k))
    println(("  t2[1,1,1] = " t2[1,1,1] ", f(t2) -> " f(t2)))
  end
end
===== u08_plane.fss
(* u08: planes and permuted views of a rank-3 array.  APL needs k⌷[2]t (a plane
   as a MATRIX, so the rank-2 overload family applies to it) and 1 0 2⍉t (an
   axis permutation).  u07 established that Array3 is the rank-3 member of the
   dispatch family; this asks what the library gives as views and what has to be
   written by hand, the way AplRow is written by hand for a matrix row
   (base/AplCore.fss:375).

   (a) what the library offers: t.shift and the bracket subarray
   (b) a hand-written plane view that IS a Matrix[\RR64,a,b\]
   (c) a hand-written 1 0 2 transpose view that IS an Array3
   (d) reshape n x 16 -> n x 4 x 4 through the flat row-major order, and back
   (e) t.plane(k) -- the Array3 trait has no such method; the `plane` at
       FortressLibrary.fss:2680 is a local function inside asString.  The call
       is the last line so that the rest of the probe runs first.

   One false start, u08_plane.out.0: the view objects' get/put/init0 first named
   their index parameter `t`, which collides with Matrix's own transpose method
   t() --
     u08_plane.fss:12:9: Variable t is already declared.
     u08_plane.fss:13:9: Variable t is already declared.
     u08_plane.fss:14:11: Variable t is already declared.
   The reach of a dotted method declaration includes every object that extends
   the trait (basic/declarations.tex:441-452), so a view object may not use any
   of its supertrait's method names as a parameter name.  Renamed to `ix`. *)
component u08_plane
import AplCore.{...}
export Executable

f(x: RR64): String = "rank 0"
f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): String = "rank 1, " |v| " elements"
f[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = "rank 2, " r "x" c
f[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): String = "rank 3, " a "x" b "x" c

(* (b) the plane view, six lines, exactly the shape of AplRow *)
object AplPlane[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], k: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,a,b\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i,j) = ix; base.get((i,j,k)) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32), v: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ix; base.put((i,j,k), v) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32), v: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ix; base.init0((i,j,k), v) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,a,0,b\] = array2[\U,a,b\]()
end

(* (c) 1 0 2⍉ *)
object AplPerm102[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\])
        extends Array3[\RR64,0,b,0,a,0,c\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (j,i,k) = ix; base.get((i,j,k)) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), v: RR64): () = do (j,i,k) = ix; base.put((i,j,k), v) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), v: RR64): () = do (j,i,k) = ix; base.init0((i,j,k), v) end
    replica[\U\](): Array3[\U,0,b,0,a,0,c\] = array3[\U,b,a,c\]()
end

run(): () = do
    t = array[\RR64\](2,3,4).fill(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 =>
                                     1.0 ((i 100) + (j 10) + k))
    println(("t = " t))

    println("(a) the library's own routes:")
    s = t.shift((1,0,0))
    println(("  t.shift((1,0,0)) moves the ORIGIN: s[1,0,0] = " s[1,0,0]))
    u = t[(0,0,1)#(2,3,1)]
    println(("  t[(0,0,1)#(2,3,1)] = " u))
    typecase u of
        Rank3 => println("  the one-deep slice is STILL Rank3, not a matrix")
        else  => println("  the one-deep slice is not Rank3")
    end

    println("(b) a user plane view that IS a Matrix:")
    p = AplPlane[\2,3,4\](t, 1)
    println(("  AplPlane(t,1) = " aplShow(p)))
    println(("  f(plane) -> " f(p)))
    p[0,0] := -1.0
    println(("  after plane[0,0] := ¯1, t[0,0,1] = " t[0,0,1] " (it writes through)"))

    println("(c) the 1 0 2 transpose as a view:")
    q = AplPerm102[\2,3,4\](t)
    println(("  q.sizes = " q.sizes))
    println(("  t[1,2,3] = " t[1,2,3] ", q[2,1,3] = " q[2,1,3]))
    println(("  f(q) -> " f(q)))

    println("(d) reshape n x 16 -> n x 4 x 4 and back:")
    n = 2
    m = aplMat(n, 16, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 ((i 16) + j))
    c3 = array[\RR64\](n, 4, 4)
    for i <- seq(0 # n), j <- seq(0 # 4), k <- seq(0 # 4) do
        c3[i,j,k] := m[i, (j 4) + k]
    end
    println(("  c3[1,2,3] = " c3[1,2,3] ", m[1,11] = " m[1,11]))
    println(("  f(c3) -> " f(c3)))
    back = array[\RR64\](n, 16)
    for i <- seq(0 # n), j <- seq(0 # 4), k <- seq(0 # 4) do
        back[i, (j 4) + k] := c3[i,j,k]
    end
    println(("  back[1,11] = " back[1,11] ", f(back) -> " f(back)))

    println("(e) t.plane(1), the library method that does not exist:")
    println(("  t.plane(1) = " t.plane(1)))
  end
end
===== u09_result.fss
(* u09: dispatch on a FUNCTION'S RESULT.  APL's rank operator f⍤1 applies f to
   each row of a matrix and then assembles: a vector of results if f returned
   scalars, a matrix if f returned vectors.  On a rank-in-the-type library the
   assembling step must therefore be chosen by the rank of the FIRST result,
   and f is an untyped host lambda (gaps.md row 59), so the question is whether
   overload resolution reads that rank off the value.

   (a) f returns a scalar  -> the RR64 assembler, a vector comes back
   (b) f returns a vector  -> the Vector assembler, a matrix comes back
   (c) the same with f a lambda whose body itself dispatches on rank

   Two false starts, both in the assembling code rather than in the dispatch:
   u09_result.out.0 subscripted an `asif`-ascribed vector,
     Unexpected method value {...}:OverloadedFunction when invoking method _[_]
     given receiver (__DefaultVector[\RR64,4\] asif Vector[\RR64,4\])
   and u09_result.out.1 called .get on it,
     ** bug! MethodClosure get(i:I):E ... has neither body nor def instanceof
     Method
   Both disappear when the ascription is replaced by a call to a typed helper
   (aplNth below), which is the same rank dispatch again. *)
component u09_result
import AplCore.{...}
export Executable

(* the typed helpers that replace `asif`: each is chosen by its argument's rank *)
aplScal(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplNth[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], j: ZZ32): RR64 = v[j]

(* the two assemblers, overloaded on the RANK of the first result *)
assemble[\nat r, nat c\](r0: RR64, f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = do
    v = aplVec(r, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 =>
                      if i = 0 then r0 else aplScal(f(aplIxRow(m, 1.0 i))) end)
    "vector: " aplShow(v)
  end

assemble[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](r0: Vector[\RR64,s\], f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String = do
    out = aplMat(r, |r0|, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 =>
                              if i = 0 then r0[j]
                              else aplNth(f(aplIxRow(m, 1.0 i)), j) end)
    "matrix: " aplShow(out)
  end

(* g computes the first result and hands it to assemble; nothing here says
   which assembler will be used *)
g[\nat r, nat c\](f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): String =
    assemble(f(aplIxRow(m, 0.0)), f, m)

run(): () = do
    m = aplMat(3, 4, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 ((4 i) + j))
    println(("m = " aplShow(m)))
    println("(a) f returns a scalar, +/ on the row:")
    println(("  " g(fn (v) => aplSumLast(v), m)))
    println("(b) f returns a vector, ⌽ on the row:")
    println(("  " g(fn (v) => aplRev(v), m)))
    println("(c) f is a lambda that itself dispatches on rank, ×2:")
    println(("  " g(fn (v) => 2.0 × v, m)))
  end
end

# APL in Fortress: the ladder

The question is not whether APL can be written in Fortress but how far the specification's syntax-extension mechanism and the library carry it before something gives, and what exactly gives. The method is the one the microGPT work settled on: each step is bounded, every probe is kept with its output, every negative claim is gated by an attempt to achieve the thing, and every new language fact goes into `gaps.md` here in the merged ledger's row format for a later merge.

The rungs follow the chapters of Stefan Kruger's "Learning APL" (https://xpqz.github.io/learnapl/), read in order; the reader climbs by reading the chapter, the exploration climbs by making that chapter's examples run inside `apl⦇ … ⦈` and agree with the book's printed results or with an oracle. One directory per rung.

| rung | chapter | what it needs from Fortress | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | It's arrays all the way down (`array.html`) | arrays, strands, scalar extension, `⍳ ⍴`, reductions, rank | done twice: 26 of 26 checks over 18 of 28 examples pass on the **native-array base**, 10 out of scope (nested arrays, `]box`, `⎕` names), plus 18 of 18 beyond the chapter; `rung-1/REPORT.md` prices that base against v1's and keeps the 21 probes `r01`-`r16` behind it. The first run, on v1's runtime-rank library, is `v1-probes/ (the probes and reports of the retired first library, kept because gap rows cite them; the library itself is in git history only)` |
| 2 | Indexing (`indexing.html`) | bracket indexing, `⌷`, index origin | done twice: 25 of 25 checks over 19 of the 40 examples pass on the native-array base (the goldens call only 5 "core"), same 19 and same 25 as v1, nothing regressed; 21 out of scope (16 nested `m`, `⎕`/`]`, tacit `⌷⍨∘⊃⍨⍤`, characters); 21 of 21 beyond the chapter. APL names are now **lambda parameters**, assignment is an **in-place put** on the library's own mutable arrays, and a row or column is a **view that is a `Vector`**; `rung-2/REPORT.md`. The workspace-table version is `v1/rung-2/`, the variables-only study `v1/rung-2b/` |
| 2b | Indexing again, variables only | APL names as **real Fortress variables** | done: the lambda route of the paper's design works — an `Id` gap as a lambda parameter binds, the name needs no `⍎(…)` escape, and host code in the block reads it; 52 of 52 checks, the chapter's variable examples run both by lambda binding and over host-declared cells, which also recovers rebinding and the cross-block session; costs a closed name set (1 grammar line per name) because a reference cannot be a gap. Layout: `base/` holds the library and grammar the rungs share (`AplCore.fss` with its API, `AplSyntax.fsi` with the grammar), grown rung by rung; `rung-N/` holds that rung's examples as a Fortress component, its expected results, its probes with outputs, and a short `REPORT.md`; `goldens/` holds the book's examples with their printed results per chapter, and the oracle's results where an oracle exists; `gaps.md` is the running gap table.

The base was **replaced once**, on 2026-09-13. The first library (rungs 1, 2 and 2b) carried one `value object AplArr(shape, data)` with the rank as run-time data and dispatched every primitive on a string; it was an interpreter nested inside the interpreter and taught nothing about Fortress, so it was retired on 2026-09-13 (git history before 0ff5eae27); only its probes and reports remain, under `v1-probes/`, because rows 1-35 of `gaps.md` cite them and those findings about the extension mechanism stand. It was priced against v1 before being promoted (`rung-1/REPORT.md`).

Goldens are the book's own printed outputs (Dyalog, `⎕IO ← 0`, so every index and `⍳` counts from zero), extracted per chapter under `goldens/`. GNU APL 2.0 is built in the container as a secondary oracle (`goldens/ORACLE.md`); it is an APL2 dialect and disagrees with 100 of the 127 outputs of the first three chapters, mostly in display and in the glyphs it lacks, so it checks values, not the book's notation.

# Rung 3 — "Glyphiary", on the native-array base

Chapter: https://xpqz.github.io/learnapl/manip.html · goldens:
`../goldens/ch3-glyphiary.md` (59 examples, the book's printed output verbatim,
index origin 0) · design: `DESIGN.md` · library and grammar: `../base/`
(`AplCore`, `AplSyntax`) · walk interpreter, JDK 25, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`,
nothing outside `explorations/apl/` touched, nothing built.

## Verdict

- **43 of 43 checks pass, over 29 of the chapter's 59 examples. Nothing fails.**
  `Rung3.out`: `checks passed: 43 of 43, over 29 of the chapter's 59 examples`.
  The 29 are Ex 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 18, 19, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36,
  39, 43, 45, 46, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59. Ten of them print more than one
  result, which is why there are 43 checks.
- **31 of 31 beyond-chapter checks pass** (`X1`-`X31`): matrix arithmetic with
  scalar extension (`X1`-`X7`), comparisons and connectives on matrices
  (`X8`-`X11`), monadic `*` and `⍟` (`X12`-`X15`), a reshape whose shape is an
  expression (`X16`), take and drop on two axes (`X17`-`X20`), commute `⍨` on a
  named function, on `⍴`, on an operator and in its monadic form (`X21`-`X25`),
  the four reductions rung 1 lacked (`X26`), residue's sign (`X27`), matrix
  catenation both ways (`X28`, `X29`), monadic `⍪` (`X30`), and a LENGTH ERROR as
  a contract violation (`X31`).
- **30 examples are out of scope**, each a `SKIP` line with its reason: Ex 1
  (`⎕IO`, `]box`, `]rows`), the 17 whose values are nested (Ex 4, 9-17, 20, 23,
  26 second line, 35, 37, 38, 49, 50), the 9 that are character arrays (Ex 3
  second line, 21, 22, 31, 32, 40, 41, 42, 52 second line), Ex 7 (`⍤` and the
  bracket axis), Ex 44 (dfns), Ex 47 and 48 (a tacit definition), and Ex 51
  (`5⍴⍨⍴m`, a run-time shape).
- **Rung 1 and rung 2 still pass on the extended base**, re-run after the library
  additions and again after the grammar additions: `../rung-1/Rung1.out` 26 of 26
  and 18 of 18, `../rung-2/Rung2.out` 25 of 25 and 21 of 21, both unchanged.
- **`DESIGN.md`'s scope list numbers several examples differently from the
  goldens**, and the goldens' numbering is what `Rung3.fss` follows. The design
  puts `⍳3 4` at Ex 19 (it is Ex 20) and `⍸` of a matrix at Ex 34 (it is Ex 26),
  and lists Ex 24, 43, 52, 56, 57 and 59 as out of scope when they are `⍸` of a
  Boolean vector, `v↑⍨1`, `∪` of a numeric vector, `~` of a Boolean vector, `⍋`
  of a numeric vector and `⊃⍋data` — all simple numeric arrays, all in scope, all
  passing. Ex 2 is reached the way rung 2 reached its two `9?9` examples: the
  matrix is bound to the permutation the book printed.
- **The rung's one new mechanism is the glyph as a value.** `AplDy` is a
  nonterminal of 31 alternatives, each an untyped host lambda, and `⍨` is two
  rules that apply it. The lambda keeps APL's rank polymorphism: the overload is
  chosen from the arguments at the call, so `v↑⍨1`, `q⊖⍨1`, `=⍨1 2 3 4 5` and
  `5⍴⍨3` all work off the same 31 lines (gap row 59). Rungs 4, 5 and 6 need
  exactly this for `/ ¨ ⍤ ∘.` and `.`.

       the top frame of a stack the caller pushes (u04_frame.out): no name is
       ever bound and no nesting can collide.  It costs about 4x a
       two-parameter call in the walker (u04 (e)).  The stack is a plain
       mutable object, so FORTRESS_THREADS=1 is assumed: two APL calls in
       parallel would share one stack.  This also gives APL's own rule that
       ⍺ ⍵ are never inherited from an enclosing dfn for nothing -- a nested
       dfn's ⍵ is its own because its call pushed its own frame.

   (2) RANK 3.  Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\] is the third member of the dispatch
       family: it reaches Rank3 and so excludes Rank1, Rank2, Number and String
       (u07_rank3.out).  There is no rank-3 analogue of Vector/Matrix -- array3
       does not route numeric elements to one (FortressLibrary.fss:2814-2819) --

       Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\].  A plane and a permuted axis order are
       six-line VIEWS, as a matrix row is (u08_plane.out).

    astk: Array[\Any,ZZ32\] = array[\Any\](1024)
    ostk: Array[\Any,ZZ32\] = array[\Any\](1024)

aplPickAt[\nat s\](i: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64

aplD1[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): ZZ32 = do (x,y,z) = t.sizes; y end

aplShow[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): String = do
    (d0, d1, d2) = t.sizes

(* dyadic ⍴ into rank 3 and out of it, cyclically over the flat row-major
   order, exactly as the rank-1 and rank-2 reshapes are *)
aplReshape3(d0: RR64, d1: RR64, d2: RR64, x: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { ((d0 >= 0.0) AND (d1 >= 0.0)) AND (d2 >= 0.0) } =
    aplArr3(aplInt(d0), aplInt(d1), aplInt(d2), fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => x)
aplReshape3[\nat s\](d0: RR64, d1: RR64, d2: RR64, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { (((d0 >= 0.0) AND (d1 >= 0.0)) AND (d2 >= 0.0)) AND (|v| > 0) } = do
    b = aplInt(d1)
    c = aplInt(d2)
    aplArr3(aplInt(d0), b, c,
            fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => v[(((i (b c)) + (j c)) + k) MOD |v|])
  end
aplReshape3[\nat r, nat c\](d0: RR64, d1: RR64, d2: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { ((d0 >= 0.0) AND (d1 >= 0.0)) AND (d2 >= 0.0) } = do
    (mr, mc) = m.sizes
    bb = aplInt(d1)
    cc = aplInt(d2)
    aplArr3(aplInt(d0), bb, cc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => do
        q = (((i (bb cc)) + (j cc)) + k) MOD (mr mc)
        m[q DIV mc, q MOD mc]
      end)
  end
aplReshape3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](d0: RR64, d1: RR64, d2: RR64,
        t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { ((d0 >= 0.0) AND (d1 >= 0.0)) AND (d2 >= 0.0) } = do
    n = (aplD0(t) aplD1(t)) aplD2(t)
    bb = aplInt(d1)
    cc = aplInt(d2)
    aplArr3(aplInt(d0), bb, cc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 =>
                aplFlatT(t, (((i (bb cc)) + (j cc)) + k) MOD n))
  end
aplReshapeM[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](rw: RR64, cl: RR64, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { (rw >= 0.0) AND (cl >= 0.0) } = do
    n = (aplD0(t) aplD1(t)) aplD2(t)
    cc = aplInt(cl)
    aplMat(aplInt(rw), cc, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => aplFlatT(t, ((cc i) + j) MOD n))
  end
aplReshapeV[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](nn: RR64, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]):
        Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] requires { nn >= 0.0 } = do
    n = (aplD0(t) aplD1(t)) aplD2(t)
    aplVec(aplInt(nn), fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => aplFlatT(t, i MOD n))
  end

(* 1 0 2⍉t as a view.  The grammar reads the three numerals, as it reads the
   rank of a reshape; every other permutation is out of scope and the contract
   says so. *)
aplPerm[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](x: RR64, y: RR64, z: RR64, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]):
        Array3[\RR64,0,b,0,a,0,c\]
        requires { ((x = 1.0) AND (y = 0.0)) AND (z = 2.0) } = AplPerm102[\a,b,c\](t)

        requires { ((aplD0(x) = aplD0(y)) AND (aplD1(x) = aplD1(y)))

    aplArr3(aplD0(x), aplD1(x), aplD2(x),

   sibling needs it *)
opr *[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    aplArr3(aplD0(t), aplD1(t), aplD2(t),
            fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => exp(t[i,j,k]))

    aplArr3(aplD0(t), aplD1(t), aplD2(t),
            fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 / t[i,j,k])

(* ------------------------------------------------- ⍤ the rank operator ---- *)
(* the typed readers that replace `asif` on a cell's result (u09) *)
aplScalOf(x: RR64): RR64 = x
aplNth[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], j: ZZ32): RR64 = v[j]
aplNth2[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 = m[i,j]

(* a cell result's shape, so that a later cell of a different shape is APL's
   LENGTH ERROR rather than a wrong answer *)
aplSig(x: RR64): RR64 = -1.0
aplSig[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): RR64 = 1.0 |v|
aplSig[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = 1.0 ((1000 aplRowsOf(m)) + aplColsOf(m))
aplSameSig(rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\]): Boolean = do
    ok: Boolean := true
    s0 = aplSig(rs[0])
    k: ZZ32 := 1
    while k < |rs| do
        (if aplSig(rs[k]) =/= s0 then ok := false end)
        k := k + 1
    end
    ok
  end

(* assemble-by-first-result: the rank of the RESULT is read off rs[0] by
   overload resolution (u09_result.out).  aplAsm1 has a one-dimensional frame,
   aplAsm2 a two-dimensional one (f⍤1 over a rank-3 array). *)
aplAsm1From(r0: RR64, rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
        requires { aplSameSig(rs) } =
    aplVec(|rs|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => aplScalOf(rs[i]))
aplAsm1From[\nat s\](r0: Vector[\RR64,s\], rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { aplSameSig(rs) } =
    aplMat(|rs|, |r0|, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => aplNth(rs[i], j))
aplAsm1From[\nat p, nat q\](r0: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\], rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\]):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { aplSameSig(rs) } =
    aplArr3(|rs|, aplRowsOf(r0), aplColsOf(r0),
            fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => aplNth2(rs[i], j, k))
aplAsm1(rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\]): Any = aplAsm1From(rs[0], rs)

aplAsm2From(r0: RR64, rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\], d0: ZZ32, d1: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
        requires { aplSameSig(rs) } =
    aplMat(d0, d1, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => aplScalOf(rs[(i d1) + j]))
aplAsm2From[\nat s\](r0: Vector[\RR64,s\], rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\], d0: ZZ32, d1: ZZ32):
        Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] requires { aplSameSig(rs) } =
    aplArr3(d0, d1, |r0|, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): RR64 => aplNth(rs[(i d1) + j], k))
aplAsm2(rs: Array[\Any,ZZ32\], d0: ZZ32, d1: ZZ32): Any = aplAsm2From(rs[0], rs, d0, d1)

(* monadic f⍤1 : the cells are the rows.  A vector IS one cell, so f⍤1 on a
   vector is f on the vector. *)
aplRank1(f: Any, x: RR64): Any = aplCall1(f, x)
aplRank1[\nat s\](f: Any, v: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Any = aplCall1(f, v)
aplRank1[\nat r, nat c\](f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Any = do
    rows = aplRowsOf(m)
    rs = array[\Any\](rows)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < rows do
        rs[i] := aplCall1(f, AplRow[\r,c\](m, i))
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm1(rs)
  end
aplRank1[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](f: Any, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Any = do
    (d0, d1, d2) = t.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](d0 d1)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < d0 do
        j: ZZ32 := 0
        while j < d1 do
            rs[(i d1) + j] := aplCall1(f, AplRow3[\a,b,c\](t, i, j))
            j := j + 1
        end
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm2(rs, d0, d1)
  end

(* monadic f⍤2 : the cells are the planes; a matrix is one cell *)
aplRank2[\nat r, nat c\](f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Any = aplCall1(f, m)
aplRank2[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](f: Any, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Any = do
    d0 = aplD0(t)
    rs = array[\Any\](d0)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < d0 do
        rs[i] := aplCall1(f, AplPlane[\a,b,c\](t, i))
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm1(rs)
  end

(* dyadic l f⍤1 r : cells paired by position when the frames agree, and a left
   argument of the cell rank itself paired with every right cell *)
aplRank1[\nat s, nat t\](f: Any, l: Vector[\RR64,s\], r: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Any = aplCall(f, l, r)
aplRank1[\nat s\](f: Any, l: RR64, r: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Any = aplCall(f, l, r)
aplRank1[\nat s, nat r2, nat c2\](f: Any, l: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r2,c2\]): Any = do
    rows = aplRowsOf(m)
    rs = array[\Any\](rows)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < rows do
        rs[i] := aplCall(f, l, AplRow[\r2,c2\](m, i))
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm1(rs)
  end
aplRank1[\nat r2, nat c2\](f: Any, l: RR64, m: Matrix[\RR64,r2,c2\]): Any = do
    rows = aplRowsOf(m)
    rs = array[\Any\](rows)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < rows do
        rs[i] := aplCall(f, l, AplRow[\r2,c2\](m, i))
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm1(rs)
  end
aplRank1[\nat p, nat q, nat r2, nat c2\](f: Any, a: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\],
        b: Matrix[\RR64,r2,c2\]): Any requires { aplRowsOf(a) = aplRowsOf(b) } = do
    rows = aplRowsOf(a)
    rs = array[\Any\](rows)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < rows do
        rs[i] := aplCall(f, AplRow[\p,q\](a, i), AplRow[\r2,c2\](b, i))
        i := i + 1
    end
    aplAsm1(rs)
  end
aplRank1[\nat s, nat a, nat b, nat c\](f: Any, l: Vector[\RR64,s\],
        t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Any = do
    (d0, d1, d2) = t.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](d0 d1)
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < d0 do
        j: ZZ32 := 0
        while j < d1 do
            rs[(i d1) + j] := aplCall(f, l, AplRow3[\a,b,c\](t, i, j))
            j := j + 1
        end
        i := i + 1
    end

(* u11: the rung-4 library half, called directly, with no grammar in the way --
   the frame stack, the rank-3 carrier, and the rank operator.  A library-only
   probe costs 15 s where a probe that uses the expander costs 25-40 s, so every
   library question is asked here first.

   (a) aplCall / aplCall1 / ⍺ ⍵ ∇, and a dfn nested in a dfn
   (b) the ⍺ contract and aplDefaultAlpha
   (c) aplBindLeft (0∘⌈) and aplTruthy over both a 0/1 and a host Boolean
   (d) rank 3: build, show, ≢ ⍴ , ⊃, reshape in and out, 1 0 2⍉
   (e) elementwise arithmetic and comparison on rank 3
   (f) the rank operator: f⍤1 over a matrix (scalar and vector results), f⍤1
       over a rank-3 array, f⍤2 over a rank-3 array, and the dyadic forms
   (g) a LENGTH ERROR from cells of different shapes *)
component u11_lib
import AplCore.{...}
export Executable

run(): () = do
    println("(a) the frame stack:")
    add = fn (): Any => aplAlpha() + aplOmega()
    println(("  aplCall(⍺+⍵, 32, 98) = " aplShow(aplCall(add, 32.0, 98.0))))
    nested = fn (): Any => do
                 inner = fn (): Any => aplOmega() × 2.0
                 aplAlpha() + aplCall1(inner, aplOmega())
               end
    println(("  a dfn in a dfn, ⍺+2×⍵ with 1, 20 = " aplShow(aplCall(nested, 1.0, 20.0))))
    (* ∇: sum ⍳n through aplSelf *)
    var sumv: Any := 0.0
    sumv := fn (): Any => do
                aplDefaultAlpha(0.0)
                if aplTruthy(0.0 = (≢ aplOmega())) then aplAlpha()
                else aplCall(aplSelf(), aplAlpha() + (⊃ aplOmega()), aplDrop(1.0, aplOmega()))
                end
              end
    println(("  ∇ recursion, sum ⍳10 = " aplShow(aplCall1(sumv, aplIota(10.0)))))
    println(("  100 sum ⍳10 = " aplShow(aplCall(sumv, 100.0, aplIota(10.0)))))
    println(("  frame depth after = " aplDepth()))

    println("(b) ⍺ absent:")
    r = try aplShow(aplCall1(add, 3.0)) catch e CallerViolation => "CallerViolation" end
    println(("  reading ⍺ in a monadic call -> " r))
    dflt = fn (): Any => do aplDefaultAlpha(-99.0); aplAlpha() + aplOmega() end
    println(("  {⍺ ← ¯99 ⋄ ⍺+⍵} 99     = " aplShow(aplCall1(dflt, 99.0))))
    println(("  57 {⍺ ← ¯99 ⋄ ⍺+⍵} 99  = " aplShow(aplCall(dflt, 57.0, 99.0))))

    println("(c) ∘ and the guard's truth:")
    relu = aplBindLeft(fn (): Any => aplAlpha() MAX aplOmega(), 0.0)
    println(("  0∘⌈ on ¯2 ¯1 0 1 2 = "
             aplShow(aplCall1(relu, aplVec(5, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => (1.0 i) - 2.0)))))
    println(("  aplTruthy(1.0) = " aplTruthy(1.0) ", aplTruthy(0.0) = " aplTruthy(0.0)
             ", aplTruthy(2.0 < 3.0) = " aplTruthy(2.0 < 3.0)))

    println("(d) rank 3:")
    t = aplReshape3(2.0, 3.0, 4.0, aplIota(24.0))
    println(("  2 3 4⍴⍳24 =" // aplShow(t)))
    println(("  ≢t = " aplShow(≢ t) ", ⍴t = " aplShow(aplShapeOf(t)) ", ⊃t = " aplShow(⊃ t)))
    println(("  ,t = " aplShow(aplRavel(t))))
    println(("  2 12⍴t = " // aplShow(aplReshapeM(2.0, 12.0, t))))
    println(("  6⍴t = " aplShow(aplReshapeV(6.0, t))))
    p = aplPerm(1.0, 0.0, 2.0, t)
    println(("  ⍴1 0 2⍉t = " aplShow(aplShapeOf(p))))
    println(("  1 0 2⍉t =" // aplShow(p)))

    println("(e) elementwise on rank 3:")
    println(("  t÷2 =" // aplShow(t ÷ 2.0)))
    println(("  ⍴(t+t) = " aplShow(aplShapeOf(t + t)) ", ⊃(t×t) = " aplShow(⊃ (t × t))))
    println(("  ,(t>20) = " aplShow(aplRavel(t > 20.0))))

    println("(f) the rank operator:")
    m = aplMat(3, 4, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 1.0 ((4 i) + j))

    println(("  ⍉⍤2⊢m =" // aplShow(aplRank2(fn (): Any => aplTrans(aplOmega()), m))))
    println(("  +/⍤1⊢t =" // aplShow(aplRank1(sumf, t))))
    println(("  ⌽⍤1⊢t (rank 3 back) : ⍴ = " aplShow(aplShapeOf(aplRank1(revf, t)))))
    println(("  ,⍤2⊢t =" // aplShow(aplRank2(fn (): Any => aplRavel(aplOmega()), t))))
    println(("  ⍉⍤2⊢t : ⍴ = " aplShow(aplShapeOf(aplRank2(fn (): Any => aplTrans(aplOmega()), t)))))
    println(("  1 2 3 4 +⍤1⊢m =" // aplShow(aplRank1(add, aplIota(4.0), m))))
    println(("  10 +⍤1⊢m =" // aplShow(aplRank1(add, 10.0, m))))
    mk = aplMat(3, 4, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 100.0)
